stem: Paediatric foreign body aspiration and ingestion are most common in children under 3 years of age. Which is the best reason for this increased risk?

options.text: They explore their environment with their mouths
They have fully mature swallowing coordination
They have a reduced tendency to place objects in the mouth
They are able to distinguish edible from inedible objects reliably
They have complete posterior dentition and chew food well

explanation: Children under 3 years commonly aspirate or ingest foreign bodies because of mouthing behaviour and developmental immaturity, including limited judgment and incomplete coordination of feeding and swallowing.
rationale: The original item was multiple-answer. It has been rewritten into a single-best-answer question with one clearly correct option.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: young children commonly mouth objects as part of normal exploration.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: swallowing coordination is not fully mature in this age group.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: children this age are more, not less, likely to put objects in their mouths.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: toddlers cannot reliably judge what is safe to eat or swallow.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect: posterior dentition is incomplete in many toddlers, which can increase risk rather than reduce it.
